facts: Octopuses have three hearts.
A day on Venus is longer than its whole year.
Al-Khwarizmi, born in Khwarazm (in today’s Uzbekistan), gave his name to the word “algorithm”.
Ulugh Beg’s observatory in Samarkand catalogued more than 1,000 stars in the 15th century.
Ibn Sina, born near Bukhara, wrote a medical encyclopedia that was studied for centuries.
Ada Lovelace wrote what is often called the first computer program — in the 1840s.
Some bamboo species can grow almost a metre in a single day.
Your brain keeps forming new connections all your life — this is called neuroplasticity.
Sharks appeared on Earth before trees did.
Sleep helps your brain store what you learned during the day.
Penicillin was discovered thanks to mould growing on a forgotten lab dish.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe.
Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
A group of flamingos is called a “flamboyance”.
Honey found in ancient Egyptian tombs was still edible thousands of years later.
The Eiffel Tower can grow about 15 cm taller in summer because metal expands in the heat.
Architects, game designers and doctors all use prototypes — small tries before the real thing.
The Silk Road linked Samarkand and Bukhara with China and Europe, carrying ideas as well as goods.
Writing something by hand can help you remember it better.
